summary: TGW IP-in-IP encapsulation + MSS clamping causing TLS record fragmentation and HTTP/2 frame split, corrupting presigned shard downloads
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 403/Range mismatch errors when fetching large sharded model artifacts from Redwood control plane. Failures correlate with network path through customer's Transit Gateway (TGW) where IP-in-IP encapsulation and an inline WAN appliance perform MSS clamping. Impact: model pulls fail during model boot, causing degraded serving and elevated latency for customer-facing inference.
impact: Model pull failures for ~20% of attempts during nightly scaling; serving nodes fall back to older cached weights, causing slower cold-start and a small percentage of inference errors.
environment_details: Private deployment with TGW-attached branch sites using IP-in-IP (IPIP) encapsulation for site-to-site tunnels. Egress path traverses branch WAN appliance that applies MSS clamping to avoid PMTU blackhole on legacy MPLS links. Control plane and object storage endpoints reachable via VPCE gateway.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Provision a serving node in customer's private deploy in us-west-2 with model gpt-large-3b-sharded pinned to version v2026-02-28.
2) Trigger a cold start by scaling from 0 -> 3 replicas during nightly batch window (large shard downloads).

3) Observe artifact presigned range GETs failing intermittently with HTTP 206/416/403 or aborted HTTP/2 stream resets in curl/nghttp2 logs when path traverses branch TGW -> appliance -> internet egress.
4) Re-run with tcpdump on serving node and packet capture on branch appliance to correlate MTU, IPIP headers, and TCP segments.
5) Reproduce is time-correlated with branch appliance applying MSS clamp to 1200 bytes for tunneled flows.
6) Disabling IPIP (or bypassing the appliance) removes the failure consistently.
logs: [serving-node] 2026-03-10T03:14:22Z GET /shards/part-12 Range: bytes=0-1048575 -> HTTP/2 stream error: PROTOCOL_ERROR (frame size mismatch)
[serving-node] 2026-03-10T03:14:23Z curl: (18) transfer closed with outstanding read data
[appliance] 2026-03-10T03:14:21Z TCP: mss clamp applied: original 1460 -> 1200 for conn src=10.1.22.5 dst=54.239.12.10 (IPIP)
[pcap] seq 0x1a2b3c TCP payload sizes: 600, 600, 300 (after IPIP header) -> observed TLS record boundaries crossing frames leading to HTTP/2 HEADERS+DATA split and nghttp2 frame reassembly error
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-10: Initial triage — customer reports shard validation failures on 0->3 scale-up. Asked for packet captures and appliance config screenshots.

Customer (DataSense SRE) 2026-03-10: Uploaded tcpdump and appliance syslogs to shared S3 (link in ticket). Note: this started after TGW attachment to new branch hub and enabling IPIP with legacy WAN appliance.

Marco Nguyen (SRE) 2026-03-11: Observed consistent MSS clamp to 1200 bytes post-IPIP encapsulation resulting in TLS records spanning multiple TCP segments. Hypothesis: TLS record fragmentation + HTTP/2 frame splitting triggers nghttp2 frame length mismatch leading to stream resets and partial range reads, which artifact client treats as corruption and retries with invalid range -> 416/403.
Marco Nguyen (SRE) 2026-03-11: Requested customer to temporarily disable MSS clamp on appliance or route traffic around the appliance. Customer agreed to test bypass during maintenance window.

Customer (DataSense SRE) 2026-03-12: Bypassed appliance for VPCE egress path during 02:00-03:30 UTC; artifact downloads completed without error for 2000+ pulls. Re-enabling appliance reproduced failures. Will coordinate WAN vendor to change clamp policy.

Marco Nguyen (SRE) 2026-03-12: Created infra PR to add additional guardrails: increase artifact client retry validation, and detect HTTP/2 frame reassembly errors to initiate TLS renegotiation fallback (gh PR #1289).
investigation_notes: Reproduced locally using network emulation: adding 20 bytes of IPIP header + mss clamp to 1200 reproduces the nghttp2 frame error under HTTP/2 multiplexed shard fetches.
TLS stack (OpenSSL 3.1) preserves record boundaries but TCP segmentization from clamp causes a HEADERS frame split; nghttp2 treats illegal split as PROTOCOL_ERROR.

S3 presigned range behaviour: partial range retries with adjusted Range header contain offset mismatches when client received truncated payload leading to validation checksum mismatch -> server 403 on second attempt (presigned token replay semantics).
No evidence of model artifact corruption on S3 side; validation failures are client-side partial-read reassembly issues.
Related to path MTU/encapsulation interplay; existing docs mention PMTU but not interactions with MSS clamps on encapsulated flows.
Customer TGW route propagation timing and traffic steering to hub appliance exacerbated the window where this surface area affected scale-ups.
resolution: Workaround: Instructed customer to disable MSS clamping for VPCE-bound flows or to adjust clamp to MTU 1350 (accounting for IPIP overhead) until WAN vendor can patch. Implemented client-side mitigations: increased HTTP/2 reassembly tolerance and added explicit detection of truncated TLS records to trigger connection restart in PR gh.com/redwood/infra/pull/1289. Post-change verification: customer reported 0 failures during bypass window and subsequent test with adjusted clamp=1350 showed successful pulls for 5000 sequential shard downloads.
postmortem_followup: Confluence runbook update: add section on 'Encapsulation-aware MSS guidance' with recommended clamp values per encapsulation type.
Cloud infra task: add an early-detection metric for nghttp2 PROTOCOL_ERRORs during shard fetches and alert at >0.5% of shard pulls per minute.
Customer-facing docs: updated Private Deploy network checklist to call out TGW+IPIP interactions and VPCE egress validation steps.
Engineering: track gh issue #1290 to harden artifact client reassembly and add a test harness that injects small MTU and encapsulation headers.
